                         LETTER OF TRANSMITTAL

                              ----------                              

                               The White House, September 14, 2026.
To the Senate of the United States:
    With a view to receiving the advice and consent of the 
Senate to ratification, I transmit herewith the Convention 
between the Government of the United States of America and the 
Government of the Republic of Croatia for the Avoidance of 
Double Taxation and the Prevention of Tax Evasion with Respect 
to Taxes on Income, with Protocol, done at Washington on 
December 7, 2022, and the Protocol between the Government of 
the United States of America and the Government of the Republic 
of Croatia Amending the Convention between the Government of 
the United States of America and the Government of the Republic 
of Croatia for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the 
Prevention of Tax Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income, done 
at Dubrovnik on April 28, 2026 (collectively, the ``proposed 
Treaty''). I also transmit, for the information of the Senate, 
the report of the Department of State, which includes an 
Overview of the proposed Treaty.
    The proposed Treaty would be the first bilateral income tax 
treaty between the United States and Croatia. The proposed 
Treaty follows the current United States Model Income Tax 
Convention, with only a few divergencies that reflect 
particular aspects of Croatian law and treaty policy. The 
proposed Treaty significantly reduces (and, in some cases, 
eliminates) withholding taxes on investment income and provides 
benefits to individuals engaged in cross-border activities 
between the United States and Croatia. The proposed Treaty 
contains comprehensive provisions designed to address ``treaty 
shopping,'' which is the inappropriate use of a tax treaty by 
residents of a third country. The proposed Treaty contains 
robust mechanisms for the resolution of disputes between the 
United States and Croatian tax authorities as well as rules 
that allow the tax authorities to provide assistance to each 
other through the exchange of information to facilitate the 
administration of each country's tax laws.
    I recommend that the Senate give early and favorable 
consideration to the proposed Treaty and give its advice and 
consent to ratification.

                                                   Donald J. Trump.
    The White House, September 14, 2026. 















































    
                          LETTER OF SUBMITTAL

                              ----------                              

                                       Department of State,
                                         Washington, July 29, 2026.
The President,
The White House.
    I have the honor to submit to you, with a view to their 
transmission to the Senate for advice and consent to 
ratification, the Convention between the Government of the 
United States of America and the Government of the Republic of 
Croatia for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention 
of Tax Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income, with Protocol, 
done at Washington December 7, 2022, and the Protocol between 
the Government of the United States of America and the 
Government of the Republic of Croatia Amending the Convention 
between the Government of the United States of America and the 
Government of the Republic of Croatia for the Avoidance of 
Double Taxation and the Prevention of Tax Evasion with Respect 
to Taxes on Income, done at Dubrovnik April 28, 2026 
(collectively, the ``proposed Treaty'').
    The proposed Treaty follows the current U.S. Model Income 
Tax Convention, with only a few divergencies that reflect 
particular aspects of Croatian law and treaty policy. The 
proposed Treaty significantly reduces (and, in some cases, 
eliminates) withholding taxes on investment income and provides 
benefits to individuals engaged in cross-border activities 
between the United States and Croatia. The proposed Treaty 
contains comprehensive provisions designed to address ``treaty 
shopping,'' which is the inappropriate use of a tax treaty by 
residents of a third country. The proposed treaty contains 
robust mechanisms for the resolution of disputes between the 
U.S. and Croatian tax authorities as well as rules that allow 
the tax authorities to provide assistance to each other through 
the exchange of information to facilitate the administration of 
each country's tax laws. An overview of key provisions of the 
proposed Treaty is enclosed with this report.
    The proposed Convention is self-executing. I recommend that 
the proposed Treaty be transmitted to the Senate for its advice 
and consent to ratification. The Department of the Treasury and 
the Department of State cooperated in the negotiation of the 
proposed Treaty, and the Department of the Treasury joins the 
Department of State in recommending that the proposed Treaty be 
transmitted to the Senate as soon as possible for its advice 
and consent to ratification.

            Respectfully submitted,
                                                       Marco Rubio.
